name: Fulafeallan

facts.text: Level 77, 30,000 health. Spawns four or five 'Part of Fulafeallan' when fought.
Ful 'foul' and feallan 'to fall'; the reading 'foul-falling' is to verify.

story:
Fuladl's twin in the low passages, or its other half: the old keepers never decided. They called it Fulafeallan, the foul thing that falls, because it drops from the roof of the passage where the water seeps through. Like its kin it is only rot that learned to move, and like its kin it comes apart under a blade and keeps coming. The keepers' last records say they bricked up the wet passage and wrote its name over the bricks, so that no one would open it by mistake. The ogres cannot read. They opened it.

The thing that falls. Fuladl's twin in the low passages, or its other half: the old keepers never decided, and wrote both names on the same wall. They called this one Fulafeallan, the foul thing that falls, because it lives on the roof of the wet passage where the sea seeps through the rock and drops on whatever walks beneath it.

The bricked passage. The hall-folk's last records say they bricked up the wet passage and wrote its name over the bricks so that no one would open it by mistake. The ogres cannot read. They opened it, looking for another storeroom, and the first ogre through the gap is part of Fulafeallan now. Like its kin it is only rot that learned to move, and like its kin it comes apart under a blade into four or five crawling pieces that keep coming. The ghosts of the hall avoid the wet passage more than any other place in Krondon, and the ogres, who do not see the ghosts, have never asked them why.
legend:
Same as Fuladl: it splits when you cut it, so kill the pieces before they reach the casters. Look up before you walk under the wet stretch of roof, because that is where it waits. One raid, one rot at a time, never both.

It hangs on the roof; if you walk under it unready it lands on the middle of the raid. Pull it from the edge of the wet stretch with a tank already in place. Some raids skip both rots and walk around the drains entirely, because the rots guard nothing a raid needs. The ones who kill them do it for the old hall-folk, who walled them away and wrote their names to warn us.

death: The roof is only stone now.

loremasterTopic.text: The foul thing that falls, the keepers called it, for it drops from the wet roof of the low passages. It is kin to Fuladl and splits as Fuladl does.

bookPage: The last records of the hall-folk say they bricked up the wet passage and wrote the name of its tenant over the bricks: the foul thing that falls. The ogres opened it looking for another storeroom. When Sir Cador had me read him the name, I looked up, and I am glad I did, because the roof above us was glistening and bulging like the belly of a fish. We woke it from the edge of the passage, as the knights of the ring-forts had told Cador to, with Sir Cador himself standing where it would fall. It fell on him. He has not forgiven any of us. We burned the pieces and went on.
